claims.text: Atomic size mismatch and chemical heterogeneity enhance lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion creates a rough energy landscape for dislocations.
The rough energy landscape forces dislocations into wavy, non-straight configurations.
Wavy dislocation configurations reduce dislocation mobility.
Fine secondary precipitates, including HCP precipitates, act as additional dislocation-pinning sites.
The combined reduction in dislocation mobility from lattice distortion and precipitates increases hardness and yield strength.
NbTaTiV can be produced as a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy by arc melting and homogenization.
Equiatomic TaNbHfZrTi is initially BCC after arc melting and casting.
Conventional casting or arc melting produces a relatively homogeneous baseline microstructure in the proposed alloys.
Hot isostatic pressing or targeted annealing can induce grain refinement.
Hot isostatic pressing or targeted annealing can promote formation and dispersion of secondary precipitates.
XRD line broadening can be used to quantify the degree of lattice distortion in the proposed comparison.
Secondary HCP phases produced by HIP can be distributed within the matrix or concentrated at grain boundaries.
At room and moderately elevated temperatures, dislocation mobility is sensitive to both lattice strain and precipitate interactions.
Processing that produces greater lattice distortion and fine precipitates will significantly increase hardness relative to the conventionally cast baseline.
Processing that produces greater lattice distortion and fine precipitates will significantly increase yield strength relative to the conventionally cast baseline.
Reducing lattice distortion or precipitate formation will lower hardness and strength.
The hypothesis should apply to chemically complex refractory HEAs with significant atomic size mismatch.
The hypothesis is limited to processing conditions that avoid excessive oxidation or contamination.
The hypothesis should hold when grain size is maintained from the nanometer to low-micrometer range.

contradictions.description: NbTaTiV is offered as an example initial alloy, but the cited NbTaTiV material has 200–400 μm grains, whereas the stated boundary restricts the hypothesis to nanometer-to-low-micrometer grain sizes.
